Editor’s note: Rob Carpenter is an independent contributor to FreightWaves. The reporting, analysis and opinions in this piece are his own and do not necessarily reflect the views of FreightWaves or its affiliates.
On July 2, 2026, a Michigan inspector pulled over a truck running under USDOT 2566250, registered to Gamboa Logistic Inc. of Beavercreek, Ohio, and by the time the stop was finished the driver had collected 11 hours-of-service violations, seven of them for tampering with the electronic logging device that exists for the single purpose of making sure a driver, a dispatcher and an inspector are all looking at the same clock. The other four were for driving past the 11-hour and 14-hour limits. Each tampering count was an out-of-service violation, meaning the truck did not move again until the driver was back in compliance.
A year earlier, on July 4, 2025, the same company filed four applications with the Labor Department to bring in 30 heavy truck drivers under the H-2B temporary worker program, at $29.78 to $31.38 an hour, for that Beavercreek worksite. The department denied all four that August. In 24 months of federal inspection data, Gamboa’s trucks ran up 13 English proficiency violations, seven of them out of service, eight drivers with no valid CDL, four driving on a suspended or disqualified CDL, a fatigue out-of-service, and a drug out-of-service. Its trucks were also involved in two crashes that killed three people, and FMCSA crash records show involvement, not fault.
The electronic logging device exists so a driver, a dispatcher and an inspector all read the same clock. The visa system exists so a company that needs workers must prove it cannot find them here and must pay a fair wage to bring them in. The Training Provider Registry exists so the person behind the wheel actually learned to drive the truck. The SBA’s pandemic programs existed to keep real businesses alive. Every one of those systems runs on the same assumption, that the company filing the paperwork is the company doing the work. This series has already followed one owner, Dragos Sprinceana, from a Gold Coast fleet FMCSA shut down in 2023 with $889,630 in penalties to a vice president’s seat at a Miami immigration nonprofit this spring, and asked who decides who sits in the seat. This piece goes looking for the seats, and at the contradiction running underneath the crackdown, that the same federal government now pulling foreign drivers out of American trucks keeps clearing and certifying the carriers that put them there, in one case a carrier FMCSA itself had already shut down.
554 Carriers, One Screen
The Labor Department publishes every employer request it decides under the PERM program, the first step in an employment-based green card, and under the H-2A and H-2B temporary worker programs, each filing naming the employer, its phone and address, the job, the wage and the outcome. I pulled every PERM filing for fiscal 2024 through 2026 and every H-2A and H-2B filing for fiscal 2024 through 2027, kept the ones for truck drivers, and matched the employers to FMCSA’s carrier census on strong signals only, the same phone and name, or the same phone in the same state. The screen returned 554 motor carriers that asked to sponsor foreign truck drivers.
Then I compared them with everyone else. Among active carriers with 10 or more trucks that FMCSA’s Safety Measurement System scores, 31.1% are in alert in at least one safety category, 17,344 of 55,823. Among PERM truck-driver sponsors of the same size, the rate is 50.4%, 57 of 113. Among H-2B truck-driver sponsors it is 48.3%. Farms that sponsor H-2A drivers to haul their own crops run at 24.3%, below the industry average. The widest gap is hours of service : 35.4% of the PERM sponsors FMCSA measures in that category are in alert, against 21.2% for all carriers with 10 or more trucks. Driver Fitness, the category that catches drivers without valid licenses or medical cards, runs 15.6% for sponsors against 8.8% for the industry.
Here is the fair concession, and it matters. A PERM filing is a request. It does not mean a worker ever entered the country, and a sponsored driver may be completely lawful. Most PERM driver petitions are for people already here who become permanent residents and get an ordinary CDL, and the non-domiciled CDL rule does not touch that path and was never meant to. Inspection records do not say which driver was sponsored, so this data does not show that a sponsored driver caused any violation. The defensible sentence is narrow: carriers that ask to sponsor foreign drivers carry these safety records. Plenty of sponsors are clean, and some of the most respected names in trucking file PERM petitions every year because they cannot fill seats.
The concentration is not random. Illinois, mostly the Chicago suburbs, accounts for 83 of 242 PERM sponsor carriers and 504 of 1,968 PERM filings. Florida’s sponsor list is mostly farms. Ohio has only five PERM sponsor carriers. The Chicago book is the same ground this series has walked from the start: Elgin, Wheeling, Mount Prospect, Elk Grove Village, Alsip, Lisle. The problem starts at the margins.
What The Rules Say Now
Three federal changes since 2025 set the stage. On June 25, 2025, the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance put English language proficiency back into the North American Out-of-Service Criteria under 49 CFR 391.11(b)(2), after the April 28, 2025, executive order, so a driver who cannot communicate with an officer is now parked, not just written up. On Feb. 13, 2026, FMCSA published its final rule on non-domiciled CDLs, 91 Fed. Reg. 7044, effective March 16, limiting those licenses to drivers in H-2A, H-2B or E-2 status, ending the use of work permits as proof, and capping the license at the worker’s authorized stay or one year. The D.C. Circuit denied emergency stays on May 5, so the rule is in force while the challenge proceeds. Read that rule next to the Labor Department data and H-2B becomes one of three remaining doors to a non-domiciled CDL, and the H-2B sponsor list is where some of this story’s worst records sit. On Dec. 1, 2025, FMCSA said it would stop letting ELD registrations flow straight from a vendor’s self-certification onto its public list and would cross-check new applications against revoked devices, acknowledging in its own words that the old system made it easier to re-register revoked devices. That is the agency describing the hole after it had been open for eight years.
Gamboa, An Aged Number And A Hypergrowth Fleet
USDOT 2566250 was added to FMCSA’s census on Dec. 18, 2014. Its only crash before 2024 lists a Miami Beach address, in 2015. Then the number goes quiet for roughly nine years, until Gamboa Logistic Inc. filed new articles of incorporation in Ohio on Oct. 4, 2023, with Mustafa Emir Yildirim as incorporator and statutory agent, and the first inspection under the revived number came in February 2024. An old DOT number matters because brokers, shippers and insurers read age as stability. A number added in 2014 clears filters a 2024 number does not. The record on file is a decade old. The company behind it is three years old.
The phone on Gamboa’s FMCSA record is a New York City number, its trucks run New York apportioned plates, and Yildirim’s other companies list a Brooklyn address, while the Ohio address carries a suite number that reads like a mailbox. On its Oct. 29, 2026, MCS-150, Gamboa told FMCSA it runs 683 power units and 683 drivers and drove more than 64 million miles. In the inspection data, 212 distinct power-unit VINs have run under the number, and those 212 tractors have also been inspected under 136 other carriers’ numbers, with 62 pieces of equipment that first ran for carriers now dead resurfacing under Gamboa. Equipment sharing is a lead, not a verdict, because trucks get sold, leased and repossessed every day. But a fleet that declares 683 trucks while showing 212 at the roadside, pulled from a pool that touches 136 other carriers, is not the single, self-contained fleet a shipper might picture, and the inspection record fairly raises the question of how much of what runs under the number Gamboa itself controls.
In the same 24 months, Gamboa logged 604 inspections, 831 violations and 25 crashes, and sits in alert in five SMS categories, with Crash Indicator, Unsafe Driving and Driver Fitness all at the 96th percentile. Its vehicle out-of-service rate is 29.2% against a 23.2% national average, and it has never been given a safety rating, even though by its own filing it puts 683 trucks on the road. The tampering is not a one-off: 11 ELD tampering counts in two years, every one out of service, including the seven-count Michigan stop, two counts in Oregon in April, tampering plus two false logs in Ohio in September, and a suspended-CDL-plus-tampering stop in Iowa on Oct. 20, three weeks before this piece was written. A crash suit, Freeland v. Gamboa Logistic Inc., W.D. La. No. 2:25-cv-01523, is pending, and whoever defends it will eventually have to produce the ELD edit history the Michigan inspector was looking at.
Polmax, The Whole Pipeline In One Building
If Gamboa is what the data looks like from the outside, Polmax is what the court record looks like from the inside. Polmax LLC, USDOT 758399, doing business as Experior Transport, operates from 12161 S. Central Ave. in Alsip, Illinois, holds a Satisfactory rating, runs 106 trucks, and is not a fly-by-night operation. It is also the largest truck-driver PERM filer in the Chicago book, 133 filings in fiscal 2025 and 2026, more than its truck count.
Follow a driver through it. Illinois job postings for Experior Transport ask for an Illinois CDL or one within 60 days of employment, the language that shows up in PERM recruitment ads. The training is in-house, with Experior Truck Driving School listed on FMCSA’s Training Provider Registry at the same 12161 S. Central Ave. address. The driver is then signed as a contractor. In Komorski v. Polmax Logistics LLC, Cook County Chancery No. 2021-CH-01601, drivers alleged they were misclassified as independent contractors, charged unlawful deductions and denied final pay, and Polmax agreed to a $1.5 million class settlement while admitting no wrongdoing. It was not the first wage case, Kawa v. Polmax LLC in 2013 named Tomasz Dulian, and Galeano v. Polmax LLC, filed in February 2025, is still open and names Dulian and Zbigniew Loszewski individually.
The ELD answer is in the Komorski file. The independent-contractor agreement filed there names Samsara Networks Inc. as the vendor for both the ELD and the event recorder, a mainstream, fully registered device. So when FMCSA data shows Polmax drivers with 16 false-log violations and 27 over-hours violations in 24 months, including eight false-log counts in one New York stop, the problem is not a rogue logbook company. The device records, and who altered any individual log the public data cannot say, which is exactly why anyone litigating against Polmax should ask Samsara for the edit history it keeps. Its HOS percentile is 90, in alert, and its trucks were cited for parking unlawfully on the roadway three times between early September and mid-October 2026. A truck on a shoulder often means a driver out of hours with nowhere to stop, which is an indicator, not proof.
Then the structure and the money. Illinois filings list Lynx Management Inc., president Tomasz Dulian, as manager of a string of Polmax entities, and a separate fleet LLC is ordinary in trucking, except it also lets the trucks sit under a different company from the one carrying the operating authority and the crash exposure. SBA disclosure data shows Polmax LLC took two Paycheck Protection Program loans totaling about $1.85 million, all forgiven, and two smaller Polmax names in the same building drew PPP money too, neither with active for-hire authority and neither inspected in 24 months. What sits in that one Alsip building is nearly every function a driver passes through: recruitment, a training school, the contractor agreement, the ELD, a separate fleet LLC holding the trucks, and the entities that drew the federal payroll money. Each of those is lawful on its own, Polmax holds a Satisfactory safety rating and admitted no wrongdoing in Komorski, and the point is not that any single piece is improper. The point is how much of a driver’s working life can run through companies tied to one address, and what that concentration means for the driver in the middle.
Certified While Shut Down
Gold Coast’s operating company, DMG Consulting, filed an H-1B labor condition application in April 2024, seven months after FMCSA put it out of service, and the Labor Department certified it in a week. That was not a one-off. MFUPRZ LLC, USDOT 2960394, has been under a federal out-of-service order since Sept. 7, 2021, with its for-hire authority revoked and a Conditional safety rating, and its last MCS-150 was filed in April 2021. On Oct. 16, 2024, three years into that shutdown order, the Labor Department certified MFUPRZ to bring in 39 H-2B truck drivers for a Dallas worksite, along with dozens of truck-driver helpers and material handlers across two states. Under the rule that took effect in March, H-2B is one of the three statuses that still qualify for a non-domiciled CDL.
An H-2B certification is a labor certification, not a CDL, and the public data does not show whether visas issued or who drove. MFUPRZ may run a warehouse or contract its drivers to another carrier, which would be legal. But the Labor Department has no field in its process that asks whether the employer is a motor carrier under a federal shutdown order, and no one at FMCSA reads Labor Department certifications. Mercator Global Logistics LLC of Elk Grove Village makes the same point in miniature: it filed 48 PERM truck-driver petitions in December 2023 while its FMCSA record showed one truck, one driver, three involuntary revocations and an inactive status. Forty-eight drivers for one truck.
The Rest Of The Chicago Book
The other names follow a pattern you can read in the inspection data. Planet Logistics, 91 trucks and 55 PERM filings, sits in alert on Vehicle Maintenance with a 34.5% vehicle out-of-service rate and 22 tire out-of-service violations. Grasshopper Trans, 30 trucks and 28 PERM filings, sits in alert on hours of service, and its 2023 MCS-150 claims about 232,682 miles per truck, when a hard-running team truck does 200,000. Profit Logistic, doing business as MP Freight, posts a 43.8% vehicle out-of-service rate. And Go To Logistics, 44 trucks and 27 PERM filings, holds a Satisfactory rating with no category in alert, and the six deaths on its record are all the Feb. 11, 2021, I-35W pileup in Fort Worth, where FMCSA credits all six deaths to every carrier with a truck in the chain. Go To had one truck in it. It belongs on the sponsor list and does not belong in the bad-carrier paragraph.
One fact cuts against the easy story. All of these carriers have a driver out-of-service rate below the 6.4% national average, Gamboa’s is 5.8% and Polmax’s is 2.4%, so as inspected, the drivers are mostly qualified on paper. The two things the company controls are hours and equipment, and those run hot. Across all 11 USDOT numbers in the sponsor workbook, FMCSA’s crash file holds 318 crashes, 13 deaths and 225 injuries, and taking out the Fort Worth pileup leaves 317 crashes, seven deaths and 139 injuries. Crash records show involvement, not fault.
The Logbook Layer
Every one of those hours violations ran through a device on FMCSA’s registered list, and that list has a structural problem that predates any of these carriers. An analysis of the registry found 178 registered devices held by 172 nominally separate companies across 28 states, all sharing a single sequential identifier counter running from 101 to 279, with the first character swapped to match the brand name in 177 of 178 cases, and the companies sharing no phones, no websites and no addresses. White labeling is legal and common, and names like TrackEnsure and ONE20 on that list have nothing to do with any of this. But 35 more registrations run on one platform identifier, PT30, under 35 company names in 20 states, almost all registered to free Gmail accounts, and when FMCSA revoked Green Light ELD in November 2025 the notice listed the model as “PT30, IOSiX.” The giveaway in the field is a driver’s record that follows the device rather than the truck, the same named driver turning up on two unrelated companies’ ELDs in different states, because the driver record lives in a shared database under the brand.
The rule that is supposed to prevent exactly this is 49 CFR 395.30 and Appendix A to its subpart, which require that any edited log entry carry an unchangeable event-status code, origin code and timestamp, precisely so a driver, an officer or a plaintiff’s lawyer can tell a legitimate correction from a cover-up. The Cook County case that put names on the problem is Owirodu v. Extra Mile International Inc., No. 2024CH06818, a class action over logbook manipulation sold to Chicago-area carriers. In a motion there, the plaintiffs’ lawyers describe two groups, a Murzac enterprise built around Phoenix ELD LLC, and a Colibri enterprise they call the “Bolt ELD LLC/Colibri ELD LLC web,” and allege both kept overwriting and deleting drivers’ hours-of-service records after a May 2025 protective order. Those are allegations in a pending case, and no one has been found liable. The motion describes a Matryoshka structure in which a registered provider swore it did not own the software platform or have access to its source code, and points upstream to a platform whose website, in the motion’s description, invited customers to “cook up” their logs. On Jan. 6, 2026, a judge authorized subpoenas to banks, payment processors and the individuals involved. One thread runs through Gold Coast itself, where records subpoenaed in that case show the federally registered Bolt ELD device carrying a support phone that rings on Gold Coast’s own RingCentral account.
The Form That Is Supposed To Make A Carrier Reachable
There is a second blind spot, and it decides what happens after a truck like Gamboa’s kills someone. Every carrier operating across state lines must file a BOC-3, naming a person or company in each state to accept a lawsuit on the carrier’s behalf. It is a one-page form that costs about $20, and its entire purpose is to make sure that when a truck kills somebody two states from where it is registered, the family’s lawyer has somewhere to send a process server. An analysis of the complete federal BOC-3 file, 1,690,743 rows covering 1,668,695 carriers, found 231,217 of them, nearly 14% of the entire federally authorized fleet, naming one of two companies operating out of a single suite in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. It found 336,458 carriers with the agent field left entirely blank, and 18,711 more who simply typed the word “Carrier” into a field FMCSA’s own instructions say only a process agent, broker or freight forwarder may fill. Ninety-two percent of Mexico-domiciled carriers in the file have no valid process-agent designation, and a spot check of 40 against FMCSA’s live authority system found 39 still cleared to run on American highways.
This is not a gap anyone has to discover. FMCSA wrote in a 2019 policy document that the designation must exist at all times for a carrier’s registration to stay valid, and that its own enforcement staff had reported being unable to complete service of process when a designation went stale. The agency put in writing seven years ago that the gate does not hold. Pair it with the equipment data and the picture is complete: the truck moves to a new DOT number within days of a revocation, and the paper trail that was supposed to make the operator reachable was never built to catch a move that fast.
The Wage Layer
The logbook and the paycheck are the same document seen from two sides. A driver paid by the mile, charged for his truck and told the violations will disappear has every reason to keep driving and no way to prove later how many hours he actually worked. Gold Coast showed what that looks like in a federal judgment: in Ealom v. Goldcoast Carriers Inc., N.D. Ill. No. 1:24-cv-05217, the court found the defendants, including Sprinceana personally, liable under the Fair Labor Standards Act and the Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act, and Anthony Ealom’s July 2023 settlement statement shows net pay of negative $2,202.08 after a $2,500 “Equipment Recovery Fee.” He finished a week of work owing his carrier money.
Super Ego is the larger version. Atkinson v. Super Ego Holding LLC, N.D. Ill. No. 1:22-cv-04127, is a putative class action alleging misclassification and unlawful deductions across a network of carriers, and a review of the inspection data turns up six carriers downstream of the Super Ego and Mimic cluster, each declaring seven or eight trucks to FMCSA while running between 170 and 260 vehicles pulled from three predecessor carriers already in litigation, all added to the census in 2024 or 2025, each identifiable from the shared-equipment pattern alone. The human version is Svyatoslav Likanov, who came to the United States from St. Petersburg. He told our reporter Clarissa Hawes that he drove car carriers for Amstel Inc. up to 140 hours a week, that dispatchers falsified his electronic logs, and that a video urging Russians to come on tourist visas steered him into the job. We reported that Amstel drivers were cited 49 times for driving without a CDL before its authority was revoked, and that Likanov and his family went into hiding after he went public. Amstel’s owners did not respond to our requests for comment. The pattern he described, recruitment through community networks, pay held back, debt that grows with every deduction, and a log that says whatever dispatch needs, is the pattern the court files describe in legal language.
The School Layer
ELDT, the entry-level driver training rule, took effect in February 2022, set a federal floor for CDL training and a registry of approved schools, and let the schools certify themselves. On Dec. 1, 2025, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced FMCSA had removed nearly 3,000 providers from the Training Provider Registry and put thousands more on notice, out of 39,554 training locations then listed. Before those removals, a match of the registry against carrier crash and network records had flagged two schools that FMCSA itself later removed on March 20, 2026. The fair concession here is large: 60% of all school-to-carrier links in the registry are simply carriers training their own drivers, like Experior Truck Driving School training for Polmax, which is legal and often the best training in the industry. The risk is the vertical, when the same group recruits the driver, trains him, employs him and, in some states, tests him, because then the federal floor depends entirely on that company’s honesty.
The Money Layer
Earlier this year I matched the SBA’s EIDL and PPP files against FMCSA’s carrier census and found $7.99 billion in EIDL loans to 85,493 carriers, including 17,631 carriers that drew $1.46 billion in EIDL loans even though their USDOT numbers were created after the program’s eligibility date. Run the foreign-driver sponsor list through the same files and 110 sponsor carriers drew 137 PPP loans totaling $50.6 million, $46.0 million of it forgiven, with 42 drawing EIDL loans and five of those having USDOT numbers created after the cutoff. Most of that money went to real fleets with real 2020 payrolls. The point is not that sponsors took loans. The point is that the same federal paperwork, a DOT number, an MC number and an insurance filing, satisfied three agencies at once, and none of them looked at what the others held.
That gap has a sharper version in the insurance file. A cross-reference of the 348 carriers insured by Compass Specialty Insurance Risk Retention Group, a Tennessee-domiciled group writing trucking liability at the federal minimum, against the SBA’s EIDL file found 65 of those carriers holding EIDL loans, and 38 Compass carriers showing a policy issued and canceled the same day, with zero power units and zero inspections, 11 of which received EIDL loans. A carrier activates authority on an insurance certificate, the certificate expires the same day, and the credential package left in FMCSA’s file matches exactly what a trucking company needs for an EIDL application. Compass and its affiliates have been in federal court on this before, in a 2020 complaint and a 2021 False Claims Act case that alleged false insurance certificates were filed with FMCSA. The United States declined to intervene, and the court dismissed both cases without prejudice on procedural grounds, so neither was decided on the merits.
How It Works
Put the layers together and a single pattern recurs across the files, a composite assembled from many carriers’ records rather than a description of any one company named above. In the abstract, it has four parts. It starts with a DOT number, ideally an old one, inherited, bought with the company that holds it, or revived behind a number that went dormant years ago. It runs on a logbook that says what dispatch needs, whether from a white-label vendor that sells “monitoring” or from a mainstream device whose records someone in the office is willing to edit. It leans on drivers who cannot push back, sponsored, indebted, paid by the mile, signed as contractors, trained in a company school, and told the violation will disappear. And it keeps the assets at arm’s length, the trucks in a fleet LLC, the authority in an operating company, the payroll money in whichever entity qualifies, so that when a crash comes, the plaintiff finds a shell and a process agent who never answers.
The inspection data shows the moves at scale. Starting from 47 seed carriers across nine known networks, including Gold Coast and Pony Express, Commontrans, Denver Cargo, AAA Freight, the Super Ego and Mimic successors, and Compass and MGR, a review of every truck they ran turned up 1,657 carriers that shared at least one vehicle, and after setting aside big fleets, lessors, one-off sales and junk VINs, 101 met the threshold for direct equipment entanglement. Leader Freight Systems declares five trucks and has run 194, and 182 of them went on to Denver Cargo. A compliance firm’s mock DOT audit this fall of two separately filed carriers put the same mechanism under a hand check, finding identical ELD login credentials used across both driver rosters, tractors and trailers interchanged between the two fleets within the same week, and one safety manager listed as the point of contact for both. Two carriers that look like competitors in the federal registry were, in practice, one operation splitting its paper trail in two. None of the individual moves is necessarily illegal. A PERM petition is legal, a company school is legal, a contractor agreement is legal until a court says otherwise, a white-label ELD is legal, and a PPP loan was legal. No carrier named in this piece has been shown to run that full sequence, and several hold clean safety ratings. What none of the federal agencies does is look at all of it at once, and the risk lives in the space between them.
What Would Close It
None of this needs a new law. The Labor Department can check every employer certification filed by a motor carrier against FMCSA’s out-of-service list, matched on the employer’s federal ID number, before it certifies, and MFUPRZ and DMG would both have failed that check. FMCSA can require every ELD registration to name its owners and its upstream software licensor under penalty of perjury, and refuse registrations that share a platform identifier with a revoked device until the licensor answers. It can treat an ELD tampering out-of-service violation as an automatic trigger for an off-site investigation, and Gamboa has 11 of them and no safety rating. It can reject a BOC-3 that names no valid process agent, or names one its own records show is stale, and refuse to keep a registration active without a real one. The Training Provider Registry can flag every provider that shares an address, phone or officer with a motor carrier and require that carrier’s crash and hours record to come with the school’s self-certification. And the SBA’s Office of Inspector General already runs a hotline, with the referral package built.
Why It Matters
The federal crackdown is aimed at the seat, and the record is about the companies that sold the seat, logged the seat and borrowed against it. This series has already told the story of Rocky Chhean, who drove for Gold Coast until the night he died in one of its trucks, and whose name the company later typed onto its registered-agent form five years after he was buried. This one ends on the drivers whose names are not in any of these records. The inspection data does not list them, the visa data does not carry them, and the court files call them putative class members. One of them sat in a truck in Michigan on July 2 while an officer counted seven tampering violations on a device that was supposed to protect him. Every system in this story, the logbook, the visa, the training registry, the process agent, the pandemic loan, was built on the belief that the company filing the paperwork is the company doing the work. For a measurable, named slice of the industry, that belief is false, and no single agency is positioned to notice.

It is based on public records, including federal court filings, FMCSA and U.S. Department of Labor data, Small Business Administration disclosure files, and state corporate records. Matters described in pending litigation are allegations only, and every person and company named is presumed to have acted lawfully unless a court has found otherwise.

Chevrolet Virtually Crashed the Silverado 92,000 Times To Make Sure It's Safe
10 photos
Photo: General Motors
Chevrolet conducted roughly 92,000 virtual crash simulations during the development of the redesigned 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 to make sure they are delivering a truck that keeps everyone safe in a wide range of real-world crash scenarios.
GM claims that its engineers were the first in the automotive industry to intentionally crash vehicles to study what happens in the impact, back in the 1930s. Nearly a century later, engineers from General Motors’ Global Safety Product Integration (GSPI) tested thousands of micro-variables, including material thickness and joint welds, occupant body sizes, and seating positions.
For a single 40-mph, 40% frontal overlap crash scenario, the team modeled hundreds of structural and restraint variations before building physical prototypes. The truck carried a 50th-percentile (average) male dummy in the driver's seat and a 5th-percentile (small) female dummy right behind him in the second row.
GM uses a family of approximately 100 full-body crash test dummies, but the number expands to 150 when classified as anthropomorphic test devices. Engineers ran 5,500 airbag tests, taking up to 100 simulations per airbag inside three environmental chambers.
Photo: General Motors Virtual models by no means replaced real-world testing entirely. General Motors still crashed approximately 50 trucks at Building 61 of its Milford Proving Ground in Michigan to verify the computer data and inspect post-crash components.
Technicians strip the interiors down to inspect individual components. They also verify that doors open easily without jamming, fuel lines remain intact, hazard and interior lights turn on, doors automatically unlock, and the OnStar emergency call connects.
Computer simulations accounted for roughly 80% of the pickup truck’s passive safety engineering work and generated nearly 2 petabytes of data, which is basically the equivalent of one trillion pages of documents.
The newly redesigned 2027 Chevrolet Silverado pickup truck features a redesigned frame with boxed sections, new tire deflectors, a collapsing steering column, and a reinforced steel safety cage to manage load paths, including changes required by the presence of an optional panoramic sunroof.
Photo: General Motors To improve rear-seat protection in frontal offset crashes, an area where the 2026 model received only a marginal rating from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS), GM added rear seatbelt pretensioners and revised the rear seat structure.
By relying heavily on AI-assisted virtual testing instead of sacrificing a large number of expensive physical prototypes right from the get-go, GM can spot weak points and improve design in terms of safety in just weeks rather than months. The auto giant deployed artificial intelligence to debug simulation models, spot structural “hot spots,” and sort through tens of thousands of data points.
The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado Crew Cab entered production this fall, while the Double Cab variant is slated to start rolling off the production line in the second half of 2027. Prices start at $41,395 (destination fee included) for the base Work Truck Regular Cab 2WD with the 2.7-liter TurboMax engine.

At the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) Conference, BMS finally revealed early data for its Alzheimer’s disease psychosis trials of KarXT, marketed as Cobenfy in schizophrenia.
Bristol Myers Squibb has finally revealed a peek at the long-awaited Phase 3 ADEPT program, showing a reduction in hallucinations and delusions in patients with psychosis associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
The data arrived Wednesday at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) Conference in Boston. BMS has been testing KarXT—approved as Cobenfy for schizophrenia—to treat complications of Alzheimer’s. The readout could represent an expansion opportunity for BMS, which picked up the asset in the $14 billion acquisition of Karuna Therapeutics in 2023.
Analysts from BMO Capital Markets were encouraged by the early efficacy signals but said investors are still awaiting more robust randomized results for the therapy. The safety data and discontinuations also left many questions unanswered, the firm noted.
Cobenfy, a muscarinic antipsychotic that combines xanomeline and trospium chloride, was approved to treat adults with schizophrenia in September 2024. Heralded as a new way to treat the difficult neurological disease, the drug has struggled on the market with side effects limiting uptake.
BMS has insisted that Alzheimer’s psychosis will provide a major boost for the product, with the ADEPT data key to establishing the market potential. Truist Securities predicted worldwide sales of $2.6 billion for Cobenfy in an October note.
“Our key takeaways are that these provide a supportive bridge to the key data readouts in 2027 particularly on preliminary tolerability and view these data as incremental as we wait for the [placebo] adjusted efficacy and detailed safety profile in 2027,” BMO said in a Wednesday morning note.

BMS’ ‘big beat’ clouded by Cobenfy, heart disease data delays
Strong quarterly results are prompting Bristol Myers Squibb to lift its 2026 outlook, though the company is facing another delay for key Cobenfy Alzheimer’s data and a pushed-back readout for milvexian.
July 30, 2026
·
4 min read

ADEPT-1 is evaluating KarXT in adults with psychosis associated with Alzheimer’s disease, with an initial 12 weeks open-label period followed by a 26-week randomized withdrawal period. The main goal is the time to relapse event during the 26-week double-blind period. At CTAD, BMS presented data from 273 patients who had completed the 12-week open-label period.
During the 12 weeks on treatment, these patients experienced improvements in hallucinations and delusion as well as disease severity, BMS said.
But more than half—56.6%—of patients experienced treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), which had been a concern among analysts. Serious TEAEs occurred in 5% of patients, with discontinuations due to these events occurring in 4.4%.
Heading into CTAD, BMO had been expecting efficacy signals but was keen to learn more about the “tolerability trade-offs.”
The readout did not include measures of the main endpoint of the trial, which looked at relapse. BMO also pointed out that the limited data was not adjusted for placebo.
“Given that this is not controlled and on the open label, we acknowledge the challenge in separating drug activity from symptom fluctuation or study participation effects,” the firm wrote. “Overall, the data support the feasibility of longer-term treatment, but in a selected rollover group. They don’t address relapse prevention, which ADEPT-1’s randomized phase will test.”
Neuropsychiatric disorders
With an approval apiece, the verdict is still out on AbbVie’s and BMS’ twin neuro buys
After emraclidine’s schizophrenia fail and Cobenfy’s laggard launch, it’s too early to know who made the better buy: AbbVie, in its $8.7 billion Cerevel takeover in late 2023, or Bristol Myers Squibb, which spent $14 billion for Karuna just two weeks later.

Tristan Manalac
Read more
The second readout presented at CTAD was for ADEPT-3 , a 52-week open-label extension of the other ADEPT programs, including ADEPT-1, with 401 people enrolled so far.
Out of 273 participants who had completed 52 weeks of ADEPT-3, the drug was “generally well tolerated” with low rates of discontinuation, BMS said. But TEAEs hit 65% of patients, including 7.7% with serious events and a discontinuation rate of 4.7%.
BMS said that symptoms like hallucinations and delusions were also improved in ADEPT-3.
The two studies were designed within the ADEPT program to initially look at patients’ response and long-term safety on KarXT, explained Cristian Massacesi, EVP, chief medical officer and head of development for BMS.
“We believe the improvement in hallucinations and delusion scores in ADEPT-1 and the long-term safety and tolerability findings shown in ADEPT-3 are encouraging as we await results from the double-blind periods of the ADEPT program,” Massacesi said.
BMS adopted a new dosing strategy in these two studies, switching from twice a day to three times a day, Truist said in October. The firm said BMS needed to show at CTAD that patients could reach effective doses without being driven off treatment due to gastrointestinal side effects.
Other trials in the program are looking at the acute efficacy of KarXT and different dosing options.
Analysts have been keenly awaiting data from ADEPT-2, which was not included in the CTAD presentation. A readout for that trial is expected in 2027 after several delays that the company has blamed on the need to recruit more patients. The study was initially expected to be ready by the end of 2025.

Biogen and AriBio reported wins for their respective therapies targeting Alzheimer’s disease, while Priavoid and Cognito Therapeutics missed the mark—though the latter plans to file for FDA approval based on a positive subgroup signal.
As Alzheimer’s disease researchers and drug developers gathered in Boston this week for the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference, the agenda was expected to focus on non-amyloid approaches to the intractable memory-robbing disease. It has not disappointed.
True to expectations, biopharma companies presented new data on therapies targeting tau—widely expected to be the next culprit of focus—but also PDE5 and even light and sound stimulation.
The conference runs through Thursday in Boston. Here are a few notable presentations so far.
Biogen’s anti-tau ASO extends benefit at 2 years
Biogen’s Ionis-partnered anti-tau therapy diranersen slowed clinical decline by 38% on a key cognitive function scale after two years, a result that strengthens the asset’s case in early Alzheimer’s disease, BMO Capital Markets said in a Tuesday evening note.
In the Phase 2 CELIA study, Biogen gave 60 mg of diranersen twice a year to 60 patients, while another 115 were randomized to placebo. From weeks 76–96, patients originally taking the antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) remained on their assigned doses, while the original placebo cohort crossed over to diranersen.
“Importantly, by Week 96, the original [placebo] cohort had received either no active treatment or only one dose and therefore served as a placebo-equivalent comparator,” Jefferies said in a Tuesday note.
The result is an improvement on 18-month results reported by Biogen earlier this year, when the regimen led to a 26% slowing of decline on the Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) in the same group of patients.
Alzheimer’s disease
Biogen takes tau Alzheimer’s therapy to Phase 3 despite mid-stage fail, prompting cautious optimism
While Biogen’s tau-targeting therapy didn’t demonstrate improvement on a dementia severity scale, the company touted biomarker and cognitive improvements from the Phase 2 study, leaving analysts eager for more data.
May 14, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
“These are highly encouraging results, particularly given the progressive nature of Alzheimer’s disease,” University of California, San Francisco’s Lawren VandeVrede, CELIA’s principal investigator, said in a prepared statement alongside Biogen’s Tuesday release . “The increasing separation observed between 18 months and two years is remarkable and clinically meaningful.”
BMO analysts appeared to agree, writing that Biogen’s CTAD update “strengthens [the] case for accumulating cognitive/functional benefits from low-dose diranersen.”
BMO added that while the improvement remains numerical and non-significant, “results support the potential of 60mg Q24W diranersen to achieve sufficient tau lowering for clinical benefit in a properly powered study.”
Jefferies agreed that the two-year data support a tau efficacy signal from low-dose diranersen. “Ultimately, the data supports advancing 60mg Q6M into Phase 3,” the analysts said.
While CELIA missed its primary endpoint, which assessed statistically significant dose response for change from baseline on the CDR-SB, Biogen in May underscored the fact that “CDR-SB results favored diranersen versus placebo across all studied doses.” Higher doses were not associated with greater slowing of decline, the company said at the time.
On Tuesday, Biogen again emphasized that clinical benefits were observed across all doses studied, with the 60 mg twice-yearly regimen showing the largest treatment effects at two years.
“CELIA gave the field its first evidence from a randomized trial that lowering tau may slow cognitive decline, and today’s two-year data suggest that benefit may build over time,” Laura Nisenbaum, interim chief science officer at the Alzheimer’s Drug Discovery Foundation, said in a statement emailed to BioSpace .
Despite the missed Phase 2 endpoint, Biogen confirmed in May that it planned to take diranersen to Phase 3.
Priavoid’s amyloid detangler fails to show benefit in Phase 2
Priavoid’s bid to detangle amyloid in the service of treating Alzheimer’s disease failed to show efficacy in a mid-stage study, the German biotech reported on Tuesday.
Postmortem findings show that Alzheimer’s is mainly characterized by neurodegeneration, along with extracellular amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles, according to the Phase 2 PRImus-AD trial ’s page on a government database. Priavoid believes that the oral asset PRI-002 “can cut the sticked substances back into small pieces,” the site reads, thereby reducing the effects of the disease.
But this benefit was not shown in the Phase 2 trial of 304 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s. Instead, PRI-002 failed to improve patients’ scores on the CDR-SB at week 48 significantly more than those on placebo, missing the study’s primary efficacy endpoint.
There was a glimmer of hope, however, as patients in a subgroup who continued in the trial for 72 weeks had between 12% and 18.8% slower decline than those on placebo, though those results also were not statistically significant. Priavoid also noted that preliminary biomarker observations, including assessments of p-tau181—a biomarker reflecting the accumulation of amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain—were “consistent with PRI-002’s proposed biological activity.”
In addition, the pill succeeded on the study’s primary safety endpoint, showing a “favorable safety and tolerability profile.”
Priavoid said in its release that the topline results “support PRI-002’s further clinical development as a potentially disease-modifying oral treatment for Alzheimer’s disease.” The company plans to present the full dataset in 2027.

This week, biopharma companies including Biogen, Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche are in Boston with new data on their efforts to tackle Alzheimer’s disease.

AriBio’s PDE5 inhibitor slows clinical decline by 31% in some patients
AriBio’s PDE5 inhibitor has achieved a rare feat: success in a Phase 3 Alzheimer’s trial.
The oral drug candidate AR1001 outperformed placebo at slowing decline in the monotherapy population, the South Korean biotech reported Monday. This met the criteria for success in a trial with dual primary endpoints, despite the drug’s failure to elicit a statistically significant effect in the overall trial population of 1,535 patients.
In the 604-patient monotherapy subgroup, AriBio’s drug slowed clinical decline by 31% compared to placebo. This result is in line with data on Biogen and Eisai’s Leqembi and Eli Lilly’s Kisunla, which achieved a 27% and 29% slowing of decline in their Phase 3 trials at 18 months and 76 weeks, respectively.
As for safety, diarrhea was more common on AR1001 than placebo, affecting 7.7% of treated participants versus 4.4% of placebo controls. This contributed to a higher rate of discontinuations due to adverse events in the treatment arm. There was no mention of amyloid related imaging abnormalities (ARIA)—a type of brain swelling associated with Leqembi and Kisunla—in AriBio’s press release, and no ARIA-like symptoms or serious adverse events were reported in the company’s Phase 2 trial .
AriBio intends to discuss the results with the FDA.

Cognito Therapeutics plans to discuss a discuss a “potential path to authorization” for its at-home Alzheimer’s therapy platform that leverages light and sound to treat the disease, despite missing the primary endpoint in the Phase 3 HOPE study.
In HOPE 3, which comprised 673 patients with Alzheimer’s, Spectris AD failed to improve thinking and daily function compared to a control group given sham headsets, Cognito reported on Monday. However, the company said a prespecified analysis of participants with mild Alzheimer’s showed a nominally significant slowing of decline on the CDR-SB, daily function and instrumental activities of daily living.
“While the HOPE study did not meet its primary endpoint, the signal in the mild Alzheimer’s subgroup raises important questions that are worth exploring further,” ADDF’s Nisenbaum said in a prepared statement. The organization backed Spectris AD.
Spectris AD uses light and sound stimulation to engage gamma-frequency brain activity. Early disruption of these waves has been linked to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 18, 2026
Collective Mining (TSX, Nasdaq: CNL) has found gold and silver in rock counted as waste inside the proposed pit at its Apollo deposit in Colombia, a day after outlining plans to spend $100 million (C$143 million) in the country next year. Of 17 holes in the shallow halo around Apollo, 15 cut intervals above the open-pit cut-off grade. All 10 holes from one drill pad hit gold and silver near surface. One cut 107.85 metres at 0.79 g/t gold and 14 g/t silver from 3.75 metres depth. A hole drilled from another pad cut 146.1 metres at 0.66 g/t gold, 19 g/t silver and 0.04% copper from 106.5 metres depth, extending below the pit floor and up to 60 metres beyond the resource boundary, Collective said Wednesday . “Overall, results suggest the pit shell understates the [shallow halo zone],” National Bank of Canada Capital Markets mining analyst Don DeMarco wrote Wednesday. Turning some of the rock already slated for removal into mill feed “could ultimately improve open-pit economics,” he said. Drilling has tested about 45% of the halo, up from 41% at the previous update, DeMarco estimated. The latest results are lower grade but cover longer intervals. Across 28 intervals in 15 holes, he calculated an average of 0.83 g/t gold-equivalent over 42.4 metres, compared with 1.18 g/t over 19.3 metres in the previous batch.
Resource update
Apollo is part of the Guayabales project about 80 km south of Medellín. Collective plans to test extensions beyond the pit next year, update the resource in late 2027 or early 2028 and complete its first preliminary economic assessment shortly afterwards. Next year’s spending would fund exploration and move Guayabales through licensing, executive chairman Ari Sussman said at a Colombian government event in New York on Tuesday. Collective aims to submit Apollo’s environmental licence application in the second half of 2027. Up to a further $1 billion in investment through 2030 depends on obtaining the licence, Colombian Vice-President José Manuel Restrepo said. Permits also stand between AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) and a much larger copper investment in neighbouring Antioquia. Its proposed Quebradona project would cost about $2.5 billion and could produce 80,000 tonnes of copper a year, corporate affairs executive Stewart Bailey said at the event. Restrepo said construction could start in 2028 if approvals come through. Collective shares dropped 7% to C$15.62 Wednesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$1.5 billion. The stock has fluctuated between C$13.81 and C$30.12 in the past year.

source_document.body:
Ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.
Why is Ford using LFP batteries for the Fathom pickup?
How do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.
Unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.
To make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Ford said it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.
The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.
Ford’s first prismatic LFP battery packs undergo final inspection (Source: Ford)
Ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.
With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford said it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its new battery energy storage business in Kentucky.
Ford EV LFP prismatic battery cell (Source: Ford)
At Ford’s new battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.
Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford said employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.
“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford said.
Covered Ford Fathom prototype at the Louisville Assembly Plant (Source: Ford)
With production testing now underway, Ford plans to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.
Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.
CEO Jim Farley said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.
Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
Farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.
Ford said the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.
The pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.
Although we have yet to see it, Ford said the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.
Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

source_document.body:
Commercial truck enforcement operations across the U.S. and Canada have uncovered hundreds of safety violations, sidelining trucks and drivers for defective brakes, unsafe tires, licensing violations and other regulatory infractions.
Recent enforcement actions in more than a dozen U.S. states and two Canadian provinces highlight continued scrutiny of commercial motor vehicles, with authorities identifying everything from improperly secured cargo to tractor-trailers operating with dangerously defective braking systems.
The operations, conducted primarily in late October and November, resulted in more than 76 drivers and 208 commercial vehicles being placed out-of-service . The operations involved state police, highway patrol agencies, local law enforcement and provincial transportation officials.
Enforcement results at a glance
The following table summarizes the reported results from the major operations in your source material.
Location | Inspections | Violations or citations | Out-of-service results
Indiana | 501 | 136 OOS violations | 85 vehicles, 51 drivers
Kentucky | 886 | 650 violations | 97 vehicles
Avon, Massachusetts | 45 | 136 violations | 7 vehicles, 11 drivers
Montgomery Pass, Nevada | 69 | 73 violations | 3 vehicles, 8 drivers
Patterson, New York | 8 | 25 tickets | 3 vehicles, 4 drivers
Norwalk, Connecticut | 12 | 10 citations | 1 vehicle
Berthoud, Colorado | Not reported | 34 violations | 2 vehicles, 2 drivers
Clearview Township, Ontario | 21 | 24 offense notices | 6 vehicles
Oakwood, Ontario | Not reported | Not reported | 2 vehicles
Pincher Creek area, Alberta | More than 30 | Not reported | 2 vehicles
Source: State and provincial law enforcement agencies, October–November 2026. Inspection totals, violations, citations and out-of-service orders are different measures and should not be added together. Kentucky’s results cover October, while Indiana’s cover Oct. 26–28.
Indiana’s Operation Guardian results in 136 out-of-service violations
Indiana State Police reported 136 out-of-service violations during Operation Guardian, a coordinated three-day enforcement initiative conducted Oct. 26-28 across 16 states.
Indiana’s Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Division conducted 501 commercial motor vehicle inspections, placing 85 vehicles and 51 drivers out of service. Eight drivers were sidelined for English-language proficiency violations.
The operation also resulted in 28 criminal arrests and 36 criminal charges, including 18 felonies and 18 misdemeanors.
Authorities seized 124.5 pounds of cannabis, 6.1 grams of methamphetamine and smaller quantities of fentanyl and other illicit substances.
Operation Guardian targeted secondary highways and bypass routes that authorities said criminals frequently use to avoid enforcement operations on major interstate corridors.
Participating states included Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee and Texas, along with Indiana.
The Indiana figures represent that state’s reported results, not the combined totals from all participating states.
Tennessee Highway Patrol troopers also identified multiple defects during a commercial vehicle traffic stop reported Nov. 10. Violations included unsecured debris spilling onto the roadway, a broken axle-position bolt, deflated trailer air bags, inoperable stop lamps and a malfunctioning turn signal. (Photo: Tennessee Highway Patrol)
Kentucky, Massachusetts report hundreds of violations
Kentucky State Police reported conducting 886 commercial motor vehicle inspections during October across its 25-county eastern enforcement region.
Troopers identified 650 violations and placed 97 vehicles out of service. The agency also conducted 115 hazardous materials inspections.
In Massachusetts, state police partnered with the Avon Police Department on Nov. 4 to enforce heavy commercial vehicle restrictions and identify unsafe trucks.
Officers weighed 150 commercial vehicles, conducted 45 inspections and identified 136 violations.
Seven vehicles and 11 drivers were placed out of service, while authorities issued $3,785 in fines.
Violations included three drivers operating without licenses, one with a suspended license, another violating a commercial driver’s license restriction and six drivers lacking medical certificates.
Inspectors also discovered two unregistered trucks and a motor carrier operating despite having failed a safety audit in 2024.
In one case, officers discovered a commercial vehicle missing brakes. Another truck was carrying so much cargo that part of its load had to be removed.
Wyoming troopers discover tractor-trailer with only two working brakes
One of the most serious mechanical violations was reported by the Wyoming Highway Patrol following a Veterans Day traffic stop along Interstate 80 east of Laramie.
Troopers stopped a tractor-trailer traveling 90 mph in a 75-mph zone on Nov. 11.
During a subsequent inspection, officers discovered 28 violations, including a braking system in which only two of the truck and trailer’s 10 brakes were functioning.
One brake chamber was completely missing, with its air lines capped. Several tires were flat or had large holes.
The driver received a speeding citation, and the tractor-trailer was placed out of service and towed from the scene.
In California, inspectors at the Highway Patrol’s Cordelia Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Facility discovered a car-hauling trailer with improperly secured vehicles.
According to the agency, two vehicles on the trailer’s lower deck were secured with only one tiedown each, while a third vehicle had no tiedown attaching it to the trailer.
Inspectors placed the transporter out of service because of the imminent safety hazard.
Tennessee Highway Patrol troopers also identified multiple defects during a commercial vehicle traffic stop reported Nov. 10.
Violations included unsecured debris spilling onto the roadway, a broken axle-position bolt, deflated trailer air bags, inoperable stop lamps and a malfunctioning turn signal.
The combination also measured 95 feet, 7 inches, exceeding the stated 75-foot maximum without the required oversize permit.
New York, Connecticut and Colorado target unsafe trucks
In Patterson, New York, Putnam County sheriff’s deputies and state Department of Transportation inspectors conducted a commercial vehicle enforcement operation along Route 22 on Nov. 17.
Of eight commercial vehicles inspected, three were placed out of service. Four drivers were also sidelined.
Authorities issued 25 tickets and made one arrest.
In Connecticut, Norwalk police partnered with state Department of Motor Vehicles police for a commercial vehicle inspection operation reported Nov. 17.
Officers stopped 12 trucks, conducted 12 safety and mechanical inspections, issued 10 citations and had one truck towed and removed from service.
Colorado authorities reported 34 violations during a commercial vehicle inspection initiative involving the Larimer County Sheriff’s Office and Colorado State Patrol near Berthoud.
Inspectors identified loose rocks, defective vehicle components, dangerously underinflated tires and damaged electrical wiring.
Two trucks and two drivers were placed out of service. Officers issued six citations and one court summons.
Meanwhile, Nevada Highway Patrol troopers conducted 69 inspections at Montgomery Pass in Mineral County on Nov. 2-3, identifying 73 violations.
Eight drivers and three vehicles were placed out of service.
Nevada Highway Patrol Commercial Troopers recently placed eight drivers and three vehicles out of service due to safety violations. (Photo: Nevada State Police)
Canadian authorities step up commercial vehicle inspections
Provincial authorities in Ontario and Alberta also conducted recent commercial vehicle enforcement initiatives.
In Ontario’s Clearview Township, provincial police and Ministry of Transportation officers conducted 21 commercial vehicle inspections Nov. 10.
The operation resulted in 24 provincial offense notices and six vehicles being placed out of service for safety-related violations.
Another Ontario enforcement operation in Oakwood, involving the Kawartha Lakes detachment of the Ontario Provincial Police and provincial transportation officials, resulted in two commercial vehicles being removed from service.
One truck had a severely defective tire that officers said should have been identified during a pre-trip inspection.
In Alberta, community peace officers from the municipal districts of Pincher Creek and Willow Creek joined Highway Sheriff Patrol personnel for a Nov. 9 commercial vehicle enforcement operation.
Officers inspected more than 30 commercial vehicles and placed two out of service.
New York targets environmental violations involving commercial trucks
Commercial vehicle enforcement has also extended beyond traditional roadside safety inspections.
New York Department of Environmental Conservation officers conducted a series of enforcement operations targeting waste-hauling trucks in Orange, Rockland and Westchester counties during October.
On Oct. 19, officers cited truck drivers transporting construction and demolition waste to a site in Tuxedo without required waste shipment documentation and registrations.
Two days later, inspectors stopped a waste-oil removal truck in Tarrytown and discovered an expired diesel emissions inspection and expired waste transporter registration.
New York Department of Environmental Conservation officers inspect a waste oil removal truck in Tarrytown, Westchester County, on Oct. 21. The company was cited for expired diesel emissions inspection and waste transporter registration. (Photo: New York State DEC)
In Rockland County, officers cited a truck driver for excessive diesel idling and leaking fluid onto the roadway.
A separate Oct. 31 enforcement operation in Yonkers resulted in 13 tickets and multiple warnings for offenses including unregistered waste transporters and uncovered loads.
The actions demonstrate how commercial vehicle operators face scrutiny not only for driver qualifications and mechanical safety, but also for environmental and cargo transportation requirements.

source_document.body:
Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines , but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.
And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.
Mountain bike power meets city bike practicality
The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).
The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.
A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.
The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a new Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.
In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.
The bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.
Two drivetrains, plenty of technology
The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.
The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.
The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.
Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.
Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.
There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.
Automatic lighting turns on as soon as the sun starts dipping, ensuring you never forget to turn on your lights
The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.
Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.
Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.
Designed for actually getting things done
Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.
Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.
The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.
The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.
There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.
The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.
As much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.
And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.
The Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.
Those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!
If you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.
Kia celebrates 40 years since launching its first EV
Kia wanted to design a new vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.
So, it created the Besta EV. The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.
Unlike the Bongo, it was developed using Kia’s in-house tech rather than sourced from another automaker and rebadged as its own.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Kia swapped the 2.0L four-cylinder diesel engine for a 35 kWh battery and electric motor, which provided a range of more than 26 miles (42 km) on a single charge.
While the Besta EV was never actually sold to the public, it laid the groundwork and offered an early glimpse at Kia’s shift to electrification.
Kia Besta EV and PV5 electric van (Source: Kia UK)
The first mass-produced Korean EV certified for commercial sale was the Kia Pride EV in 1993. In 2011, the Ray EV became Kia’s first series-production electric car.
Kia expanded its electrification ambitions to Europe and the UK in 2014 with the first-generation Soul EV, the beloved boxy, funky crossover that was discontinued after the 2025 model year.
The Korean automaker has come a long way since the Besta EV, with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from compact cars to mid-size and three-row SUVs, vans, and just about everything in between.
Kia’s EV lineup ranges from the entry-level EV2 to the three-row EV9 and PV5 van (Source: Kia UK)
Kia now offers an electric option for nearly everyone with seven-passenger EVs on sale in the UK and Europe, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 Passenger van.
With its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) and a new B-segment electric hatchback set to launch by the end of 2027, Kia has no plans to slow down. On top of this, Kia will expand its PBV lineup with the PV7 next year, a larger sibling to the PV5.
Kia reveals plans to launch its first software-defined electric vehicle (Source: Kia)
Four decades after the Besta EV arrived, Kia said it continues to “lead the pack today” with one of the most diverse all-electric EV lineups of any brand.
Through October, Kia has sold over 135,000 EVs in the UK, with fully electric vehicles now accounting for over 37% of total sales.
From left to right: Kia EV2, EV3, EV5, and EV9 (Source: Kia UK)
Thanks to its new EV lineup, Kia became “Europe’s fastest-growing top 10 passenger-car brand.” According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, Kia registered 377,078 vehicles between January and August 2026, up 9% compared to the same period last year.
Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, said the growth is thanks to having “one of the broadest and most advanced electrified line-ups in Europe.”
In the US, Kia launched the compact EV3 ( check out our review of it ) this year, starting at just $29,890. It joins the EV6, EV9, and Niro EV in Kia’s US electric vehicle lineup.

source_document.body:
DHL Global Forwarding has leased a Boeing 747 freighter aircraft and crew to provide its first-ever dedicated service for the India market, creating regular capacity connecting China, India and Europe.
The freight management arm of DHL Group ( XETRA: DHL ) announced Monday that it has launched its own-controlled freighter service between Hong Kong, Navi Mumbai airport in India and Liège airport in Belgium to support growing demand between the regions. Flights will operate twice weekly, giving shippers in China direct capacity into the Mumbai region, while opening additional capacity from India to Europe. DHL Forwarding will use its ground network to move shipments from Liège airport to destinations across the continent.
DHL Global Forwarding secured the capacity through DHL Aviation, the company’s in-house cargo airline, but the flights are being operated by an undisclosed partner carrier. DHL Aviation operates and manages a fleet of nearly 300 aircraft, including Boeing 777 and 767 freighters, but relies on former joint venture partner Polar Air Cargo and other carriers for Boeing 747 airlift.
Adding a scheduled, dedicated service supports DHL Forwarding’s broader expansion in the Indian market.
India is one of the fastest-growing air freight markets in Asia, supported by strong growth in manufacturing and exports. International air cargo volumes are growing strongly because of accelerating e-commerce demand, supply chain diversification away from China and the growth of advanced manufacturing capacity, with high-value and time-sensitive products leading the way. East Asia is a major source of components for products made in India. On the export side, India is shipping large amounts of pharmaceuticals to Europe and North America, including higher-value complex generics, biosimilars and next-generation therapies. India has also emerged as an alternative source of active pharmaceutical ingredients, according to Boeing’s latest air cargo forecast.
The DHL service is expected to support customers in industries such as life sciences and healthcare, technology and electronics, engineering and advanced manufacturing.
The Boeing 747 freighter offers about 100 metric tons of capacity per flight. DHL Global Forwarding is initially targeting around 25 to 30 metric tons per flight for the India sectors, or about 55 tons per week, with potential to grow as demand develops.
“India is a strategic market for DHL Global Forwarding and an increasingly important part of our global air freight network,” said Henk Venna, global head of air freight, in a news release. “With this new dedicated service, we are strengthening connectivity between China, India and Europe and providing our customers with reliable capacity and greater access to key growth markets. This expansion reflects our long-term commitment to India and to supporting our customers as their trade flows grow.”
DHL Global Forwarding said it plans to further expand its dedicated connectivity between India and Europe with a new Bengaluru-Europe service in March.
“This is not a one-off addition. It is part of our broader ambition to build a stronger air freight bridge between India and the rest of the world. The new Mumbai service, followed by Bengaluru-Europe, demonstrates our confidence in the Indian market and our ambition to grow alongside our customers,” said Venema.
DHL is not alone among integrated logistics companies building up capabilities in India. FedEx in August announced plans to invest $150 million to outfit a proposed air hub in Delhi, India. It previously said it would invest $250 million to equip a new air terminal at Navi Mumbai International Airport .
